title: `staticimport` checks should error in `rc-v*` branches
description:
It's easy to miss the `staticimport` checks since you have to look at a PR in just the right way to find them. That makes sense for normal day-to-day checks, but I think it's worth considering making it an error in the `rc-` branch so that we don't forget to update them.

The checks as they are now wouldn't trigger an error or message unless a function currently being statically imported was updated, and we usually have a reason for updating those static imports... so we should probably update them before pushing out a new release.

title: Spin off pkgdown workflow
description:
We currently have the pkgdown workflow contained within the `routine` workflow, but this means that you can't manually trigger a website rebuild.

I ran into an instance today where I would have liked to re-build a site manually (debugging flexdashboard).

title: Roll out `lock-threads` across shinyverse
description:
#20 and #23 added a shared workflow for locking closed and inactive issues.

We now need to roll out the `lock-threads` workflow to shinyverse repos. The list below is not _every repo_ but the most popular repos. The count of would-be-locked issues below is valid as of 2023-07-19.

```[tasklist]
- [ ] [rstudio/shiny](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (1747 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/plumber](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (440 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/shinydashboard](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (205 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/leaflet](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (330 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/flexdashboard](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (276 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/py-shiny](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (161 closed inactive issues)
- [x] [rstudio/bslib](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (175 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/crosstalk](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (29 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/thematic](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (64 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/httpuv](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (162 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/shinytest2](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (141 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/htmltools](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (126 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/promises](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (32 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/websocket](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (41 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/webshot2](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (9 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/sass](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (41 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/gridlayout](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (12 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/chromote](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (29 closed inactive issues)
- [ ] [rstudio/learnr](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio): (282 closed inactive issues)
```

Are the repos on this list that should be removed or repos that should be added?

## Roll out questions

Once enabled, the workflow will lock 50 issues per run. This number is not configurable. The long-term goal is to run the workflow once per week (early Monday mornings). 

While the main workflow parameters are set in the shard workflow, the run schedule is set in the workflow in each repo. If we roll out the same workflow schedule to all the above repos at the same time, we'd lock 740 issues the first time the workflows run, tapering down from there.

Should we roll out the workflow...

* ...slowly across repos (starting small and working up), once per week?
* ...to all repos and just take the notifications hit?
* ...with an initial schedule that runs daily or staggers our repos across all days? And then follow up with a second rollout that moves to the weekly schedule?
* ...to close much older issues, e.g. 365 * 2 days, and then roll out waves to reduce issue age?

title: Reporting a vulnerability
description:
Hello!

I hope you are doing well!

We are a security research team. Our tool automatically detected a vulnerability in this repository. We want to disclose it responsibly. GitHub has a feature called Private vulnerability reporting, which enables security research to privately disclose a vulnerability. Unfortunately, it is not enabled for this repository.

Can you enable it, so that we can report it?

Thanks in advance!

PS: you can read about how to enable private vulnerability reporting here: https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/security-advisories/repository-security-advisories/configuring-private-vulnerability-reporting-for-a-repository

title: Routine feature request: shrink png images
description:
It'd be helpful to add an action that

* Installs `optipng`
* Runs `optipng` on a list of directories provided to the action
* Commits any updates to those files back to the repo

The actual code might look something like this:

```bash
# Shrink images in man/figures
sudo apt-get install optipng
optipng man/figures/*.png
git commit man/figures/*.png -m "Shrink images in man/figures (Github Action)" || echo "No changes to man/figures/*.png"
```

but it'd be extra helpful to allow an array input of directories.

```yaml
- name: Shrink pngs
  uses: rstudio/shiny-workflows/shrink-png@v1
  with:
    paths:
      - man/figures/*.png
      - vignettes/**.png
```

Current cadence:
* Restores from cache using `actions/cache`
* Install Library
* test / possibly cause failures
* On successful testing, save to cache

Wanted cadence:
* Restore from cache using `actions/cache/restore`
* Install library
* Save to cache using `actions/cache/save`
* Test / possibly cause failures

R-CMD-check.yaml: expose an `error-on` input
description:
## Request

Expose an `error-on` input on the reusable `R-CMD-check.yaml` workflow and forward it to `r-lib/actions/check-r-package`, so a calling repo can decide that a NOTE fails the build.

## Why

`R-CMD-check.yaml` calls the action without setting `error-on`:

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-workflows/blob/main/.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml#L263

```yaml
      - name: Check package
        uses: r-lib/actions/check-r-package@v2
        with:
          working-directory: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}
          check-dir: '"check"'
          args: 'c(${{ inputs.extra-check-args }}, "--no-manual", "--as-cran")'
          build_args: 'c(${{ inputs.extra-check-build-args }}, "--no-manual")'
          ...
```

The action's `error-on` [defaults to `'"warning"'`](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/v2/check-r-package/action.yaml), so **a NOTE always passes CI** and there is no input to change that. `extra-check-args` doesn't help — that's `R CMD check` arguments, not `rcmdcheck`'s `error_on`.

A package that is NOTE-free and wants to stay that way therefore can't enforce it in CI through this workflow. NOTEs are how R CMD check reports undeclared imports, `:::` on another package's internals, and stale documentation — the class of thing that is cheap to fix immediately and expensive to find later.

The pre-check hook (`.github/shiny-workflows/check.{sh,R}` via `internal/run-local-script`) isn't a workaround: it runs as the step *before* `check-r-package`, so it can't influence that step's inputs.

## Suggested shape

```yaml
      error-on:
        type: string
        default: '"warning"'   # unchanged behavior for every existing caller
        required: false
```

forwarded as:

```yaml
          error-on: ${{ inputs.error-on }}
```

Defaulting to `'"warning"'` keeps every current caller byte-identical; only repos that opt in change behavior. Same YAML-quoting convention as the existing `extra-check-args` / `check-dir` inputs.

## Caveat for callers

Worth a line in the input description: `'"note"'` can be flaky in CI even for a locally-clean package, because of environment NOTEs like *checking CRAN incoming feasibility* and *checking for future file timestamps*. That's a reason to make it opt-in per repo, not to default it.

## Context

Came up in posit-dev/shinyreact, which just reached a NOTE-free `R CMD check` and gated it locally with `devtools::check(error_on = "note")` — but CI still passes on a NOTE, so the gate is only half real. Tracked on our side in posit-dev/shinyreact#195.
